instruction: Identify available flights from Singapore to Tokyo on the upcoming Monday.

metadata.explanation: Task variation 1: Flight search from Singapore (SIN) to Tokyo (TYO) on next Monday. Uses the same URL parsing evaluation pattern to verify correct origin/destination airports and departure date. Reuses existing framework functions without requiring custom implementations.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic is correct: get_active_tab_url_parse can extract fromStation, toStation, and departing (renamed to time) from URL query parameters
Rule processing is correct: get_rule_relativeTime converts 'next Monday' to absolute date format {Year}-{Month0D}-{Day0D}
Metric logic is correct: check_direct_json_object compares extracted parameters against expected values
Coverage is complete: All instruction requirements verified (origin=SIN, destination=TYO, date=next Monday)
Minor issue: Airport code 'TYO' is a city code - Tokyo has multiple airports (NRT, HND). Some airlines may use specific airport codes instead of TYO, which could cause false negatives
Minor issue: The evaluator only checks URL parameters, not actual page content, but this is acceptable for URL-based verification pattern
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider accepting multiple Tokyo airport codes: Allow 'TYO' OR 'NRT' OR 'HND' for toStation to handle different airline website implementations
Consider case-insensitive matching for airport codes to improve robustness
The rule_validation_issues error appears to be a false positive - the actual JSON correctly uses type='rule' (line 61), not 'rule_relativeTime'
